stem:
A 36-year-old attends her GP to discuss a routine clinician-collected Cervical Screening Test. HPV16 is detected, but the reflex liquid-based cytology is negative. She has no abnormal bleeding or other symptoms.

What follow-up is recommended under the Australian screening pathway?

options.label: A
options.text: Return to routine screening in 5 years
options.explanation: Routine five-year screening follows a low-risk result. HPV16 detection places her in a higher-risk pathway despite negative cytology.

options.label: B
options.text: Repeat HPV testing in 12 months before considering referral
options.explanation: A 12-month follow-up pathway can apply to selected non16/18 HPV results with low-risk cytology. It is not the pathway for HPV16 detection.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HPV16 carries sufficient risk to require colposcopy regardless of the negative reflex cytology. Colposcopy determines whether biopsy and treatment are needed.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Repeating cytology alone would fail to follow the HPV-based higher-risk pathway. A negative cytology result has already been obtained and does not remove the referral indication.

options.label: E
options.text: Refer directly for cervical excisional treatment
options.explanation: HPV16 positivity alone does not establish a lesion requiring excision. Colposcopic assessment and appropriate histology guide treatment.

context: HPV16 or 18 detection requires colposcopy referral even when reflex cytology is negative.
